Recent 30-day forecasts and ensemble runs cluster maxima in the 24–27°C range, with limited cold-front influence keeping values from dropping to typical winter lows near 23°C or below. Traders appear to weigh these factors against forecast uncertainty, placing the highest probability on the upper end of the near-term model consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Istanbul's August 4 maximum temperature centers on 28°C and 29°C as the most probable outcomes, reflecting closely balanced ensemble forecasts from global models.** These probabilities capture the narrow range expected under persistent high-pressure conditions that favor clear skies and daytime warming, tempered by the moderating influence of the Bosphorus and Black Sea. Recent model consensus points to a peak near 31–32°C in broad guidance, yet local station measurements and urban heat island effects often run 2–3°C cooler, pulling implied odds toward the lower end of that range.

Key differentiating factors include subtle shifts in surface wind direction—northerly flows enhance marine cooling, while lighter or southerly components allow greater insolation and higher maxima—and the precise timing of peak heating relative to the daily observation window. With resolution hinging on official meteorological service readings, traders monitor updated model runs for any adjustments in thermal advection or boundary-layer moisture that could tip the daily high across the 29–30°C threshold. Historical August variability in the region further underscores the sensitivity to these short-term atmospheric details.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Ongoing heatwave conditions across southeastern Korea, driven by the expansive North Pacific High, position daytime highs near 33–35°C as the leading outcomes for Busan on August 4.** Official KMA observations recorded 39°C on August 1 amid severe heat warnings, with similar patterns persisting into early August as warm, humid air masses dominate. Coastal sea breezes and high humidity moderate extremes, while model consensus from short-range forecasts (e.g., timeanddate and AccuWeather) points to highs around 32–33°C (89–90°F) under partly cloudy skies. An approaching tropical depression (KMA TD No. 24) is forecast to track northwestward by August 4, potentially increasing cloud cover and moisture that could suppress peak temperatures below recent peaks. These factors, combined with typical post-Changma variability and historical August baselines of 29–32°C, underpin the market-implied odds favoring 34°C at 37.5% and 35°C at 25%. Updated KMA briefings and model runs over the next 48 hours will refine steering patterns and any intensification effects.
